items.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: About a month later Mingus called me up and said, “Would you like to do a date?” I said “sure.” I went there, and the nucleus of the Composers Workshop was there, and that’s the way Mingus’ Jazz Workshop records came into play.

ctx.x: About a month later, well that was the last concert we did, and it was just too much for me. I was the musical director of it and just kind of controlling all of these various human elements was just beyond me, I’d had enough of it. So I said look, somebody else can handle this, I’ll just play in it. And it just kind of fell apart. About a month later Mingus called me up and said, “Would you like to do a date?” I said “sure.” I went there, and the nucleus of the Composers Workshop was there, and that’s the way…
And you along the way picked up degrees from, was it Manhattan School of Music?
Yeah. It was a hell of a lesson. But I wrote it in quarter/quantotriplets.
Yeah, I assumed so, yeah, yeah. I have to listen to that again. Did you have any problem with -- that band was only partially a jazz band, wasn't it?
Yeah. Art Farmer, John LaPorta Porter --
